title: Closed form
summary: A widely used but non-universal label for formulas considered explicit relative to an allowed vocabulary of operations/functions.

content.human: “Closed form” usually means an explicit formula, but what operations are allowed differs by field and author.
content.exact: QEVA Protocol 0.1 assigns no universal predicate ClosedForm(E). Any claim that an expression is “closed form” must declare the permitted expression language or cite a contextual convention.
content.example: a_n=2^n may be called a closed form for the recurrence a_{n+1}=2a_n, a_0=1 when exponentiation is allowed.
content.caveat: Treating “closed form” as one globally defined mathematical property would create false precision.

relations.note: Explicit formulas are often compared with recurrence representations.

verification.method: Definition checked for internal consistency; not yet linked to an external formal proof artifact.
